claims.text: Dynamic strength and ductility in solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn are governed primarily by the temperature and strain-rate sensitivity of dislocation slip and cross-slip.
High lattice friction and solid-solution strengthening modulate the dynamic mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn.
Phase transformations and twinning are not the primary mechanisms governing the tested dynamic behavior.
Increasing temperature or decreasing strain rate increases dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
Increased dislocation mobility lowers strength.
Increased dislocation mobility increases ductility.
Low temperature or high strain rate restricts dislocation motion.
Restricted dislocation motion at low temperature or high strain rate raises strength.
Restricted dislocation motion at low temperature or high strain rate reduces ductility.
The proposed FeNiCrMn specimens can be prepared as a homogenized, single-phase FCC alloy with minimal pre-existing defects and secondary phases.
Local lattice distortions, stacking-fault energy, dislocation density, and dislocation mobility mediate the mechanical response.
Strong solid-solution strengthening in the high-entropy FCC matrix raises lattice friction and impedes dislocation motion.
Thermal activation at higher temperature or lower strain rate facilitates dislocation glide and cross-slip.
FeNiCrMn has moderate stacking-fault energy that suppresses twinning and phase transformation.
Yield strength will increase as temperature decreases or strain rate increases.
Ductility will decrease as temperature decreases or strain rate increases.
No abrupt mechanical-response changes caused by twinning or phase transformation will occur from 77 K to 600 K and from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi exhibits similar dynamic-response trends attributed to dislocation mechanisms.
The presence of Co causes CoCrFeMnNi to have slightly different absolute mechanical-property values from FeNiCrMn.
The proposed mechanism applies only to coarse-grained, single-phase FeNiCrMn without significant secondary phases and not to severely deformed, nanostructured, or multiphase variants.

contradictions.description: The mechanism affirmatively assigns moderate stacking-fault energy and consequent suppression of twinning, while the uncertainty field says the stacking-fault energy and its effect on twinning propensity are not established.

The specimen is variously called 'as-solidified, homogenized,' 'solidified, homogenized,' and 'as-solidified or homogenized.' Strictly, an as-solidified specimen has not undergone homogenization, so the intended initial processing state is ambiguous.
